finding: The MAF housing, not the intake brand, decides the MAF Scaling option. A Race preset (PRL Race, 27WON Race) only goes with that Race housing. A street, HVI or stock-size housing keeps Factory. An intake whose tube or housing diameter differs from stock (Injen, MAP and similar) throws fueling and knock control off and needs a real calibration. One owner lost about 7 mpg on a wrong-diameter intake until he swapped it.
basis: Primary (KTuner staff on its own presets, 6 posts across 2019-2023) + Consensus (owners on T1/T2)
ktuner_setting: MAF Settings > AFM Flow (owners' 'MAF Scaling': Factory / PRL Race / 27Won Race / Custom)
log_channel: STFT B1 + LTFT B1 at warm cruise, MAF Hz (not logged yet)
notes: Adds KTuner-staff primary sources to a card currently sourced to vendor and forum text. civic11forum-75 ('big intakes need a tune' vs 'PRL HVI needs none') is the same rule seen from both sides: it depends on the housing size. 27WON says its own machined housing keeps trims within ~1.5 % of OEM (vendor, T2). PRL Cobra street housing needs no MAF change (T2 owner).

finding: The 10th-gen non-Si 1.5T MAF reads in volts, and KTuner once had calibrations only for the Si's frequency MAF. The 11th-gen FE's AFM Flow is in Hz (103 points, 2,031-10,000 Hz) and ships Race presets. Per-voltage corrections from 10th-gen videos don't carry over.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help: AFM Flow converts 'voltage or frequency' to g/s) + Data (owner's map file: MAF_Scaling_* on a Hz axis) + one FE1 owner editing 'MAF Scale (in Hz)'
notes: caraddict's per-voltage numbers (-8 % at 0.98 V and so on) are a 10th-gen manual car: the method carries over, the numbers never do.

finding: How owners rescale at part throttle. Log warm part-throttle driving and average the total trim at each MAF breakpoint. Move g/s by the same sign and size (STFT trend -2 % means -2 % on g/s, so a positive trim raises g/s). Drop lift-off and coasting rows, where fuel cut makes the trims read 0 or spike. Drop throttle transients too: a larger housing shows 10-11 % trims on throttle changes that settle to 1-2 %. Reach the upper bins with a slow roll-on rather than stabbing the pedal. Repeat until the trims sit within about ±3 %.
basis: Physics (a positive trim means the ECU added fuel because measured air was too low) + KTuner staff (T3: '+30 % in one area means that section is lean') + Forum (method)
kb_relation: extends kc-maf-data-rules; confirms kp-which-way-a-fuel-trim-points-when-correcting-the-airflow-cur (ready to promote to a card)
ktuner_setting: MAF_Scaling_Custom (AFM Flow), ≤ maf_step_max_pct 10 %/round, curve strictly rising
log_channel: MAF Hz, STFT B1, LTFT B1, TPS, MAP, ECT
notes: Caveats: the T2 videos are on a manual car ('tall gear'). On our CVT, use S mode with a steady roll-on. On this car trims freeze at 0 above about 8 psi MAP (g3-05), so bins used under boost can't be corrected from trims. Brake override blocks the brake-and-throttle steady-load trick on modern cars.

finding: Owners zero the LTFT min/max ('Fuel Trim Limits') while MAF logging, so all correction shows in STFT. That is a map change and only reaches the car by a Flash, because real-time edits are temporary. Our app sums STFT + LTFT, so the trick isn't needed.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help: Fuel Trim Limits set the STFT/LTFT ranges; real-time edits must be reflashed to stay)
kb_relation: new (answers the open question in forum-afr-maf-research.md §1 #11: 'do I need to flash it?' Yes)
ktuner_setting: Closed Loop Settings > Fuel Trim Limits (out of scope: not an editable table)
notes: Don't propose it: it changes a table outside editable_tables and adds a Flash for nothing.

finding: This car's ECU goes open loop under boost. On all 4 owner drives with boost, STFT B1 reads exactly 0.0 on 100 % of warm rows at 12 psi MAP or more (360 rows), 99 % at 10-12 psi and 89 % at 8-10 psi, against 16-43 % below 8 psi. LTFT holds a fixed value there. KTuner's Closed Loop Settings put open-loop entry on a TPS threshold by default, or on a MAP threshold ('WOT Based On MAP Only'). So full-throttle mixture comes from the AFM Flow curve alone, and cruise trims say nothing about it.
basis: Data (owner's TunerView logs aug22-0903, aug30-1529, aug30-1601, sep01-0813: STFT B1 by MAP bin) + Primary (KTuner Help, Closed Loop Settings; KTuner staff: STFT is zero in open loop)
kb_relation: extends kc-open-loop-wot (its 'not confirmed for this car' is now settled by this car's logs)
ktuner_setting: Closed Loop Settings (open-loop engagement TPS / WOT Based On MAP Only / WOT MAP Based Engagement): read-only
log_channel: STFT B1, LTFT B1, MAP, TPS
notes: What changes in the app: (1) an AFM Flow bin correction must use only rows below ~8 psi MAP with STFT not frozen at 0, or the zeros pull the correction toward nothing. (2) WOT mixture is judged only against AFR Command / the map target, never from trims. The boundary is 8-10 psi MAP or TPS ≥ 40-70 %; which input KTuner uses on this ECU isn't confirmed. Script: scratchpad/stage2/ol.py.

finding: A MAF Scaling change also moves the knock picture. Lowering the g/s values lowers the load the ECU computes, so the ignition and knock tables are read at a lighter load. One owner got part-throttle knock after lowering MAF values, and slightly rich scaling helped. Another saw his Knock Control floor rise from 0.49 to 0.64-0.70 over eight MAF tunes, back to 0.49 on stock. Don't add a blanket % for a housing-diameter change.
basis: Physics (AFM Flow g/s → mg/stroke load → ignition/knock table lookups) + Data (one T2 owner's logs) + Forum (search summary)
log_channel: Knock Control, Knock Retard, Ignition, STFT B1/LTFT B1
notes: T2 cars, so the size isn't ours. The mechanism is general. Our maf_step_max_pct (10 %) limits the size of a step but doesn't watch knock: the Shakedown after an AFM Flow Flash should read Knock Control against the Baseline, not trims alone.

finding: KTuner staff say base tunes don't change MAF scaling or part-throttle ignition. MAF needs rescaling only for a housing or intake-flow change. If the mixture isn't reaching AFR.CMD, or the trims have to intervene, the MAF scaling is what needs adjusting: fix the MAF curve before touching AFR targets.
basis: Primary (KTuner staff, T2 1.5T Accord and T3)
ktuner_setting: AFM Flow before WOT Enrichment; AFM Fuel (mg/stroke → pulse) is left alone
notes: ktuner-forum-55 is a speed-density K20 analog ('enrichment targets only reach target if the base fuel tables are right'): same logic, different table.

finding: On the 1.5T KTuner calls the full-throttle mixture table 'WOT Enrichment', and its load axis is MGStk (mg per stroke, a loggable channel). 'Nominal Lambda For Component Protection' and 'Minimal Lambda Setpoint' are KTuner Help pages under the 2017+ Civic Type-R (Bosch) section, not 1.5T table names. Some platforms also have a 'WOT Enrichment Cat Heating' table, and the AFR.CMD channel shows which one is active.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help table of contents lists both pages under '2017+ Civic Type-R'; KTuner staff tell a 1.5T Accord owner 'see the WOT Enrichment tables in your table list')
kb_relation: contradicts kc-table-wot (its '(KTuner calls it Nominal Lambda for Component Protection)'; same wording in fact-check.md §1 row 6 and afr-tuning-research.md §2 Step C / §3)
ktuner_setting: WOT_Enrich_L / WOT_Enrich_H = KTuner 'WOT Enrichment' (Low/High cam), load axis MGStk
log_channel: AFR.CMD; mg/stroke channel if TunerView offers it on this ECU
notes: It's a name, not a number, but it's the label the owner looks for on screen. Also closes a gap: afr-tuning-research §3 says the WOT_Enrich load axis is missing. Its unit is mg/stroke, so logging mg/stk would let the app judge mixture cell by cell. Confirm the exact label on the owner's KTuner screen. Version 1.0.11.9 changed the 'WOT fueling target strategy' for 2023+ Integra (same engine): watch for the same on 22+ Civic tunes.

finding: KTuner flex fuel: an ethanol sensor through a converter (0.5 V = 0 %, 4.5 V = 100 %) on ECU pin E54 (Secondary ECT input), with P2185 and P0128 disabled. Three scalers by ethanol %: Fuel % (normally left at default), Ign Adj % (scales the 'Ethanol Ignition Adjustment' map, RPM × MAP) and PSI Adj % (scales 'Ethanol Boost Target Adjustment', RPM × TPS). KTuner warns that a CVT puts out more torque on ethanol even without extra timing. Without a sensor these tables add nothing, so pump E10 gets no ethanol timing or boost.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, Civic/Accord Flex Fuel Tuning; vendor product pages)
log_channel: Ethanol (not on the owner's logger; not needed)
notes: Flex fuel itself is not ours (no sensor, no E85). The part that fits is the E10 answer: no flex table acts on E10, and the closed-loop trims handle E10's +4.3 % fuel, as kc-e10 says. Ethanol maps add up to +5° (T2 owner).

finding: The AFR KTuner shows is the factory front wideband's lambda times 14.7, on any fuel. TunerView labels it 'Wide Band' and the owner's CSV calls it 'O2'. It is not an external sensor. On E85 a target of 0.80 λ reads 11.8 on that scale. A reading of 29 when revving is fuel cut.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help item abbreviations: 'Wideband - Factory Wideband Value') + Physics
kb_relation: confirms kc-rich-wot; confirms kc-e10 (fact-check §1: what's shown is the real lambda)
notes: Ties the owner's CSV column 'O2' (unit AFR) to KTuner's 'Wideband'.

finding: Short-term trim swings by design: -10 to +15 % between acceleration and cruise looks normal (KTuner staff), and +7 to -11 % was judged normal with a race MAF tune. Long-term or averaged total trim is the number to judge. The forum line for LTFT is ±10 %, with single digits at steady state.
basis: Consensus (≥3 T2 sources incl. KTuner staff) + Data (this car: warm-cruise STFT sd 2.1-2.5 %, total trim median -0.8 %)
notes: Our ±5 OK / ±10 Stop applies to warm-cruise total trim, which matches. Spikes over +20 % on lift-off and +6 % at idle show on stock tunes too (T3 Si): they are filtered rows, not findings.

finding: A beginner's rule that 'STFT of 5 % or more is bad' and that 10.6 AFR at full throttle is very rich and will hurt the catalyst.
notes: Refuted by KTuner staff (STFT -10/+15 % normal, civicxi-134) and by this car: WOT 10.1-10.7 on every drive with pulls, against a map target of 11.0, on the safe side. Worth having so the agent can calm an owner who read it.

finding: Trim pattern → cause, beyond the preset mismatch. Large positive LTFT after an intake: unmetered air (MAF seal, MAF leak, vacuum line), a dirty MAF, injectors, or an exhaust leak upstream of the front sensor. Large negative trims: a Race preset on a non-Race housing, leaking injectors, or a boost leak (metered air escapes after the MAF, so the mixture goes rich). Test on the basemap or stock file to separate tune from hardware.
basis: Physics + Primary (KTuner staff: 'either a boost leak or a RACE MAF tune without a RACE MAF') + Forum
log_channel: STFT B1/LTFT B1 by MAP band; Turbo Pressure vs Turbo Pressure Target
notes: A boost leak gives negative trims, which complements fact-check §6 ('a vacuum leak would give positive'). On this car trims freeze above ~8 psi (g3-05), so a boost leak shows as negative trims only at light positive-pressure cruise (0-8 psi) and as underboost plus richer-than-target AFR at full throttle.

finding: A damaged catted downpipe (cat substrate breaking up) on a 10th-gen CVT came with extreme rich trims and P0172; LTFT returned to 0 ±2 % after stock parts and a replacement pipe.
basis: Forum (one owner, several parts changed at once)
kb_relation: new (doesn't contradict kc-downpipe: that card is about flange leaks, this is a failed cat, and the evidence is confounded)
notes: Not used: several parts were swapped together.

finding: Full-throttle open-loop AFR can differ by about 10 % between the first pull and later ones. A Honda tuner says it depends on whether the car and sensors are at operating temperature, so WOT AFR comparisons need matched conditions. Another owner found 'slightly rich under full boost' acceptable on a vendor tune.
basis: Forum (T1, incl. a pro tuner) + Data (this car: WOT AFR spans 9.5-10.5, 9.8-11.3, 10.0-10.5 and 10.3-10.8 across four drives)
notes: Supports judging the mixture per drive against the map target, warm, not across drives.

finding: A Civic FE1 CVT owner (Turkey, E5, KTuner V1.2) aimed for WOT 11.3-11.4 by editing MAF Scale (Hz). He sees 10.6 at tip-in, then 11.3-11.4, with spikes to 11.7-11.8. Aiming leaner puts spikes about 0.4 AFR past the aim.
basis: Data (one T1 owner's log, same model and gearbox)
ktuner_setting: AFM Flow top end (out-of-scope (context): the WOT lever is locked)
notes: Same car and gearbox, different fuel (E5). On our rules, 11.7-11.8 against an 11.0 target is past Watch (0.5 leaner). It's a concrete reason to keep the lever locked and to require AFR Command before any top-end MAF work.

finding: An 11th-gen Si (KTuner + TSP Stage 1, intake, intercooler, DP/FP) went into limp above 4-5k rpm with a flashing CEL and no codes. DI fuel pressure (DIFP) sat near 16 against an 18 target. Lowering the tune's maximum fuel output parameter fixed it.
kb_relation: confirms boost_step_gates.difp_min_pct (data/thresholds.json) and the fuel-pressure Safety channel
ktuner_setting: vendor 'max fuel output' parameter (out-of-scope); our map: DI_Fuel_Pressure_Target_* forbidden
log_channel: DIFP, DIFP Target (both on the owner's logger)
notes: 16/18 = 89 %, just under our 90 % DIFP gate, so the gate would have flagged it. Higher-power Si map, so a 21 psi Starter is unlikely to reach the pump's limit. The rule stands as a symptom → cause: DIFP falling below target at high rpm under boost means fuel supply, not tune finesse.

finding: Owners disconnect the battery for 30 minutes to clear a post-flash emissions warning or 'reset fuel trims'. KTuner says codes can be cleared with the unit, so the battery disconnect isn't needed.
basis: Primary (KTuner staff) vs Forum folk practice
ktuner_setting: KTuner toolbar / TunerView: read and clear codes
notes: Inference, not checked: a disconnect also wipes the learned Knock Control and trims, so the next drive starts like an after-flash drive.

finding: Downpipe codes on the 11th gen: P0420 (catalyst efficiency) and P2A01 (rear O2 sensor range/performance), plus P0138/P0139 on the 10th gen. In KTuner: Main Parameters → Disables/Monitors, with boxes for catalyst efficiency, O2 slow response, O2 performance and post-catalyst rich/lean (P2096/P2097). Some codes have no box (staff: none for P0139/P0159/P0400 on one platform; an owner: none for P2A01). KTuner says these are for off-road use only, and staff won't advise disabling emissions equipment. Unplugging or deleting the rear O2 makes the ECU run rich, set codes or go limp. A disable box is the route owners use. One owner kept P0420 away for about 2,000 miles on a richer vendor tune; a spacer plus a mini-cat cured it for another.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, Disables/Monitors; staff) + Consensus (T1 owners)
ktuner_setting: Main Parameters → Disables/Monitors: 'P0420 – Catalyst Efficiency', O2 slow response, O2 performance, P2096/P2097 post-cat lean/rich
notes: This car's map already has P2096/P2097 and P0128 disabled and keeps P0420 on (downpipe-power-research §3 screenshot). 'Richer tune keeps P0420 away' is one owner's guess: never a reason to enrich.

finding: The 'no-code' downpipes don't always stay quiet. TSP says its downpipe throws no code, and a PRL HVDP owner had no CEL in about 5k miles. But an 11th-gen owner on an RV6 downpipe (with its built-in spacer) got P2A01 twice. A TSP high-flow downpipe owner gets an intermittent 'Emission systems' CEL in heavy rain or after 30+ min of highway (code not read). A PLM catted pipe throws a code even with Hondata.
basis: Contested: vendor claim + 1 owner 'no CEL' vs 2 T1 owners with codes (Forum, no logs)
kb_relation: contradicts kc-downpipe-catted-catless ('400-cell TSP and RV6 claim no warning light, and owners report none')
log_channel: none: read codes after wet and long-highway drives
notes: The RV6 pipe's cell count is not stated (older RV6 pipes were 300-cell). The TSP case is condition-based and the code unread. vendors-58 is the 27WON 200-cell pipe sold by TSP ('CEL if not tuned'), which matches the card. Fix: soften 'owners report none' to 'most owners report none; a few report a rear-O2 code (P2A01) or a wet-weather CEL'.

finding: US owners say: put the stock downpipe back and clear codes a month before inspection, or flash back to stock and unlock KTuner before a dealer visit. That works only where inspectors read OBD readiness. Vietnam's đăng kiểm (QCVN 85:2025) tests tailpipe CO/HC/λ and checks that the warning lamp lights at key-on and goes out. No source says inspectors read OBD monitors.
basis: Primary for the Vietnamese rule (QCVN 85:2025 via downpipe-power-research §3); the owner advice is US practice
notes: In Vietnam the risk is the tailpipe gas test (catless) and the 65-75 M VND fine for an unapproved modification, not a readiness monitor. The app shouldn't repeat the 'clear codes before inspection' trick.

finding: P0046 (boost control circuit range/performance) on 11th-gen Si high-boost maps (TSP map 2/3, 21-23 psi), under hard mid-rpm acceleration, with power steering, cruise and lane-assist warnings. Causes owners found: a sticking wastegate actuator (the replacement set to about 1.3 V DC closed) and a pinhole leak in the vacuum line on the charge pipe between throttle body and intercooler. A new downpipe only seemed to fix it for a while.
basis: Forum (2 T1 owners, multimeter readings, no logs)
log_channel: EWG Position vs EWG Target, Turbo Pressure vs Turbo Pressure Target (all on the owner's logger)
notes: Si 6MT at higher boost than ours. civic11forum-72's theory (stock downpipe elbow) is refuted by the same owner's later finding. civic11forum-17 ('aggressive turbo response wore out the actuator') is the owner's guess. Matches owner-voices #9: the electronic wastegate linkage is a known weak point. A log check: EWG Position not following EWG Target, or boost under target with the wastegate shut.

finding: P0299 (underboost) and Boost Target Dampening. KTuner says disabling Boost Target Dampening (Quick Enables) requires disabling P0299 (Disables tab), or it sets at low throttle. With dampening off, the logged TC Target never drops to atmospheric, even at closed throttle. On a CVT KTuner says to also set Boost By Gear to protect the gearbox. A 2024 non-Si 6MT on Starter 21 + TSP had dead-pedal limp episodes that he tied to an enabled P0299 monitor in Quick Adjustments.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, Disable Boost Target Dampening) + one T1 owner
ktuner_setting: Quick Enables → Disable Boost Target Dampening; Disables → P0299 Underboost; Boost_By_Gear_Limits
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target (at closed throttle), Turbo Pressure
notes: Dampening is one reason this car's logged target tops out at 19.2 psi against 21 (kc-table-boost). Disabling it is out of scope on this CVT. A Flash readback gets a free check: a Turbo Pressure Target that never falls to atmospheric at closed throttle means dampening is off. The owner's P0299 story is one case and unconfirmed.

finding: After a flash: dash and module warnings during the flash are normal, and driver-assist warnings can stay until the car has been driven, usually 10-15 minutes. After 100 %, turn the key off for at least 10 s, back on, and wait for 'flash successful'. A CEL right after flashing: key off, wait, key on without starting, accept the KTuner prompt and let it finish. Firmware 21 adds 'Clear All Module Errors After Flash'. Limp after a flash: read the codes from the KTuner toolbar or TunerView first.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, Flashing: What To Expect; staff) + Consensus
kb_relation: new (owner-voices §2 #10 asks for this help card); extends kc-after-flash
ktuner_setting: Flash; Clear All Module Errors After Flash
notes: A help card, never a Verdict. Pairs with kc-after-flash (Knock Control starts high) and kc-shakedown.

finding: The wrong codebase gives error codes after a flash (U0301 on a 2016 Civic 1.5T): start a new tune with the codebase that matches Tools → KTuner Unit Info, or the other version when a basemap offers two. If your factory calibration isn't listed, pick the closest ECU number or send the ECU scan to support. The CVT hatch's ECU number differs from the sedan's.
ktuner_setting: File → New Tune (codebase); Tools → KTuner Unit Info
notes: The U0301 example is a 10th gen. The rule (codebase must match the unit info) is general.

finding: Module and network codes after tuning: U129E is a communications error and doesn't change fueling. Disabling U0122 removes a CAN error but also disables the sport-mode button. If sport mode won't engage after a dual-tune flash with VSA not disabled, a module has a code or something external is wrong.
notes: Help-desk material only.

finding: P0128 (coolant thermostat) and P2185 are disabled for flex fuel on the secondary ECT input. P0128 after a tune can also be a stuck-open thermostat: flash stock to test. This car's map already has P0128 disabled, so a failing thermostat shows only in the ECT log (slow warm-up, coolant sagging at cruise).
basis: Primary (KTuner Help) + Forum + owner's map screenshot (downpipe-power-research §3)
notes: The app already checks 'engine warm, coolant ≥ 80 °C'. With P0128 off, an ECT that never reaches about 80 °C on a long drive is the only warning.

finding: KTuner's channel names vs this owner's TunerView CSV, and what the app detects. KTuner's list: K.Cont (Knock Control), K.Ret (Knock Retard, °), K.Count, K.Cycle, A.Ignition, TC.Target (turbo target), TC.Press (turbo pressure), EWG.Duty / EWG.Posi / EWG.Target, DIFPress / DIFP.Target, Wideband (factory), TPS / TPS.C (commanded), IAT 1&2, ECT 1&2, STFT/LTFT 1&2, Ethanol. Owners say 'K.Con'. The owner's CSV uses long names: Knock Control, Knock Retard, Ignition, Turbo Pressure, Turbo Pressure Target, EWG Position, EWG Target, DIFP, DIFP Target, O2, TPS, TPS Command, IAT, IAT2, STFT B1, LTFT B1, MAP, ECT, Transmission Temperature, Gear, Speed. It has no AFR Command, MAF Hz or mg/stroke. KTA.detectChannels finds the long names but misses K.Cont, K.Con, K.Ret, TC.Target, TC.Press, DIFPress, STFT1 and LTFT1, and would read TPS.C as TPS.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, Item Abbreviations) + Data (owner CSV header in data/example-*.js; detectChannels run against the abbreviations)
log_channel: all; missing: AFR.CMD, MAF Hz, mg/stk
notes: App gap: a CSV exported from the KTuner PC software (.kdlg → CSV) may carry the abbreviations (not confirmed). It would then lose Knock Control, Knock Retard, boost, DI pressure and trims, and every safety line would read Can't tell. Add the aliases to engine/kta-engine.js CHANNELS (k.cont|k.con → kControl, k.ret → knock, tc.target → boostTarget, tc.press → boost, difpress → fp, stft ?1 / ltft ?1 → stft/ltft, tps.c → tpsCmd). The official list has no AFR.CMD or MAF entry, but KTuner staff refer to an 'AFR.CMD item in the data list'. Whether TunerView offers AFR Command / MAF Hz on the FE ECU is still unconfirmed. TPS vs TPS Command on this car: under boost TPS reads 52-94 while TPS Command reads 92-100, so 'TPS' behaves like the driver's request and 'TPS Command' like the plate (inference from data). TPS Command reaches 99-100 on pulls, so the '95 % cap on CVT international ECUs' some owners report isn't present here. IAT/IAT2: under boost IAT reads 3-6 °C above IAT2 on every drive (fact-check §4: IAT after the intercooler, IAT2 before the turbo); see conflicts-g3.md.

finding: Knock gauges: on the 1.5T watch Knock Control (K.Cont), not Knock Count. Knock Retard is logged rounded (3.8° shows as 3.5) and actual ignition is rounded to whole degrees on OBD platforms. One owner saw the on-screen knock value frozen while the log kept changing.
notes: civic11forum-29 adds one point to kc-log-gate: a frozen gauge on screen doesn't mean a frozen log, so judge from the CSV.

finding: Boost channels. TC.Target is the commanded boost (the owner's 'Turbo Pressure Target'). TC.Press is read at the turbo, before the throttle; MAP is read at the manifold. KTuner logs both as absolute (subtract ambient for gauge boost; the owner's CSV already shows gauge psi). Once spooled, TC.Press and MAP should sit close to TC.Target, and a boost leak shows across all three. Final Boost Target is a table cap, not a channel.
log_channel: Turbo Pressure, Turbo Pressure Target, MAP, EWG Position
notes: Gives the app a check from channels it already has: on a floored pull with the plate open, Turbo Pressure well above MAP means a restriction or partly shut throttle. Underboost with EWG Position near shut means a leak or the turbo's limit (owner-voices #9). The civicx-27 source is a search summary, but civicxi-99 is KTuner staff in full.

finding: This car has one bank. LTFT1 never reads -100 % unless LTFT2 was picked by mistake, and an 'LTFT -100 throughout' log is invalid, not a fault. KTuner logs STFT/LTFT for banks 1 and 2.
notes: App gap: detectChannels' /\bltft\b/ also matches 'LTFT B2'. A trim column pinned at -100 or +100 should be Can't tell ('bank 2 or a dead channel: log Bank 1'), never a trims Stop.

finding: TunerView logging habits. Start recording before the run, because the Bluetooth link to the V2 isn't always reliable. A blinking indicator top-right means it is logging. Log through the gears at full throttle to catch boost. The TunerView CSV is separate from on-board logs and drops extended channels. A .kdlg is what KTuner software and forum readers review (a TunerView export can be renamed .kdlg). From the phone you can flash stored maps, log, and read or clear codes. The V1.2's Bluetooth PIN is the last five digits of its serial. Tutorials are in the TunerView section of KTuner Help.
notes: One line for the brief: start the TunerView log before you leave, check the blinking indicator, then export the CSV.

finding: Extended CAN data (V2 'Ext CAN' Type 1 for 2016+ Civic: steering angle, Lon.G, Lat.G, brake pressure, clutch position, four wheel speeds) is blocked from the OBD port by the CAN gateway on newer cars. That explains why this car's 'Acceleration' channel reads 0.0 on every row.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help V2 Extended Data; KTuner staff 2024, Civic platform)
notes: Don't ask the owner to fix it in the logger: no setting brings it back.

finding: On-board and auto logging (V2 / KTunerECU) start and stop on rpm, TPS, MAP and speed thresholds. With the defaults it starts at once and never stops. Erasing on-board logs takes up to 2 min. V2 LEDs can alert on coolant or knock-count thresholds, and LED boost thresholds are entered in millibar absolute.
kb_relation: confirms ktuner-only-tuning.md §1 (on-board logging with activation windows)
ktuner_setting: On Board Logging Activation Window; LED setup
notes: The owner logs with TunerView on a phone, so this is context only.

finding: TunerView Lite runs on a rooted Honda head unit (sideloaded APK). Version 1.5 added CSV, GPS and a log viewer, and 1.6.6 added CVT temperature. Most aftermarket Android head units can't hold the Bluetooth link.
notes: Not this owner's setup.

finding: On The Fly Map Switching in practice. Cruise must be fully off. Hold Cancel 2-3 s; the tach shows 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000 rpm for Tune 1 / 2 / 3; Resume/Set changes it and a long press confirms. Unplugged, the car boots in Tune 1 (valet). A plugged-in V2 restores the last-used tune at power-on. To log the right tune, plug in first, start, then check or select it. ECUs without OTF support run only Tune 1. Boost By Gear is shared by all three tunes. The flashed tune stays when the device is unplugged. V2 tune slots (whole files) are not the three OTF tunes, and moving between slots is a re-flash, not on the fly.
ktuner_setting: On The Fly Map Switching; V2 Flash menu (tune slots)
log_channel: none (no channel records the tune: owner tags Map slot); tach reading at selection
notes: Slot count: owners say 5 (civicxi-130, youtube-41/111), KTuner Help says 10 plus factory (firmware-dependent; Help wins). Matters for Map slot tagging: with the V2 left plugged in, a drive runs the last-used tune, not Tune 1.

finding: 'The car defaults to map 3 at startup when no OBD device is connected.'
notes: KTuner Help: without the unit the car boots in Tune 1 (ktuner-official-45). TSP also keeps factory boost in map 1 for valet. Said in the same video as correct cruise-button steps.

finding: Flash power and procedure. Put a battery charger on the car (or drive a long way first) and set the laptop to high performance: failed flashes are usually voltage. Ignition ON, engine OFF, and never flash with the engine running, which can brick the ECU. A flash takes about 3-10 min. After 100 %, key off, then on. A V2 Touch needs a high-power USB port, at least 4.3 V, or it browns out and resets: power it from the OBD port. 'Low Voltage on Pin' means the ECU refused the flash, usually the cable.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help, staff; TSP about its own process) + Consensus
notes: Together with g3-24 and g3-39 this makes one help card.

finding: Recovery. A failed flash puts the ECU in recovery mode and the car won't start: reconnect and say yes to recover, and it returns to the factory software. But a Recovery prompt while the engine is running means a loose OBD cable dropped some data requests: don't press yes, or it starts a recovery flash to factory. A 1.5T that won't start or connect after a vendor flash is probably in recovery. 'Factory Software Hasn't Been Setup Properly' means the tunes were cleared: set up the factory tune with the unit off the car.
notes: The 'don't press yes while running' line is the most useful one.

finding: Lock and unlock. A KTuner unit locks to the first ECU it flashes, and registering and locking need the internet. Before selling: Return To Factory, then Unlock Unit From ECU (screenshot Reflash Info → KTuner Units as proof). Never buy a locked unit; support covers current owners. Server timeouts show as 'Exchange incomplete' or a lock loop. A blinking blue V1.2 with the key on is unlocked and working. A vendor tune needs the serial and software number from Tools → KTuner Information.
ktuner_setting: Tuning → Return To Factory → Unlock Unit From ECU
notes: Help-desk material, not tuning.

finding: An upload isn't a flash. Saving a tune to a V2 slot doesn't put it on the ECU, and a failed flash silently recovers to factory. KTuner diagnosed a dual-tune Si peaking at 17.5 psi in both modes as 'not on a tune', and said to confirm with a datalog, not the stock gauge. There is no way to see which flash is on the ECU.
kb_relation: extends kc-shakedown (and CONTEXT.md 'Flash readback' / playbook 'flash' stage)
ktuner_setting: Upload Tune vs Flash Now; V2 Flash menu
log_channel: Turbo Pressure Target, STFT B1/LTFT B1
notes: Caveat for readback on this map: the logged target never passed 19.2 psi even when flashed (dampening and ramp), so 'target reaches 21' is no proof. Readback must use the boost_step_gates pull (pedal ≥ 85 % held 4 s above 3,500 rpm) or trims after an AFM change.

finding: Real-time tuning: edits are temporary and must be reflashed to stay. On boosted cars only the low or the high cam map can be real-time at a time. A car that won't run without the laptop had real-time tuning left enabled.
notes: out-of-scope (context): the app never writes to the ECU.

finding: CAN Gateway: on cars with Honda Sensing the CAN gateway can stop a V2 from waking with the car. V2 firmware 1.0.1.16+ has a CAN Gateway Yes/No option on the main menu. Set Yes in accessory mode. Firmware updates come from KTuner software → V2 Special Commands. The V2 screen can sleep and need a replug.
notes: The 11th-gen FE has Honda Sensing, so it applies. Goes in the flashing/logging help card.

finding: KTuner has tested the V2 at unit temperatures up to 180 °F (82 °C) in Arizona: a hot parked car isn't a problem.
basis: Primary (KTuner staff about its own hardware)
notes: Reassurance for a Vietnam owner who leaves the V2 plugged in a sun-parked car.

finding: KTuner only flashes the ECU. Some newer ECU software needs the CVT module updated too, which only Honda or a shop with Honda flashing can do.
notes: 10th gen, 2019. Context only.

finding: Stacking many options in one first flash (anti-lag, 2-step, early spool, advanced VSA, no artificial knock, boost per gear) gave failed flashes (recovery) and a misfiring car. Plain Starter 2 at 21 psi with only 2-step ran fine. Another owner kept Starter 18 with moderate settings and no Early Spool.
notes: Si (same family, different calibration). One more example of one change per Flash.

finding: Quick Adjustment and Quick Enable names on the 1.5T. Throttle Responsiveness, Turbo Responsiveness, Turbo Spool, Rev Hang / Throttle Padding (the off/on transition used for rev-hang disable), Boost Target Ramp Rate (Factory Ramp, Improved Ramp 1, Improved Ramp 2, Aggressive Ramp 1, Aggressive/Disable Ramp), Normal and ECO boost targets, boost limits by gear, Early Spool, and artificial knock-control rise (non-Si, removable since 1.0.10.1). On a Starter map every quick adjustment reads Factory by default. 1.0.13.0 added more for the 22+ Si.
basis: Primary (KTuner Help / feature matrix / staff) + T1 owners naming the dropdowns
ktuner_setting: Main Parameters → Quick Adjustments / Quick Enables
log_channel: TPS, Turbo Pressure Target, EWG Position (lag test)
notes: Adds the exact Boost Target Ramp Rate option names, so 'one level up' can name the next option.

finding: Software history items: 1.0.10.0 added WOT CAM command, DI fuel pressure target and Ignition Maximum tables, a 4-bar MAP option and a race-only removal of throttle dampening at a stop. 1.0.10.1 removed non-Si artificial knock. 1.0.10.4 added CVT temperature monitoring. 1.0.11.7 added 4-bar MAP for the 11th-gen 1.5T and Si. 1.0.11.9 extended the MAP error range and changed the WOT fueling target strategy (2023+ Integra). 1.0.14.0 lowered the MAP error threshold (2025-26 Si).
notes: Context. The 1.0.11.9 WOT strategy change is the one worth watching (g3-08).

finding: Advanced VSA must be disabled for dyno runs, and turning Cruise Main on disables it. 'VSA disable' reduces VSA intervention.
notes: Context only.

finding: Auto start/stop: an owner says KTuner can disable it on his 11th gen, but KTuner staff (Oct 2023, 2023 Si software) say there's no dedicated setting, only what the parameters list offers.
notes: Probably software version or trim. Settle by looking at the owner's parameter list.

finding: On-the-fly launch control adjusts in 100 rpm steps with the clutch in and cruise off (manual cars).
ktuner_setting: On The Fly Adjustable Launch Control
notes: Manual only.

finding: Hardware prices: V1.2 $449 and V2 $649 (KTuner 22+ Civic page). V1.2 plus TunerView on a phone saves about $200 over the V2; a 10th-gen setup with a $50 tablet and the $5 app.
notes: Noise for the app.

finding: Owners prefer KTuner on this platform because it exposes more options than Hondata.
TikTok: CAPTS (KTuner Malaysia) posted a 'PoPs' feature for the 10th-gen FC1 CVT on V1.2, and a pop-tune how-to for the 11th gen was seen as a search snippet.
notes: Nothing checkable.

finding: Table-editing tips (KTuner staff): enter values directly, use Ctrl-J or Ctrl up/down, and when raising boost targets dial back the lower-rpm cells so the 3D curve stays smooth.
kb_relation: confirms kc-boost-step (low rpm only lowered, smooth curve)

finding: What a downpipe gives. 27WON's 200-cell catted downpipe on a stock tune measured +7 whp / +11 tq peak first, later +12 / +13 peak and about +8 / +9 average over 2,000-6,500 rpm. Its catted turbo-back adds +20 whp / +34 wtq on the Si. An owner says a high-flow cat gives about 20 whp over factory and catless only 3-5 whp more. Owners report quicker spool and say a tune 'really started to shine' with DP + front pipe. One noticed no sound change with the stock muffler.
basis: Primary (vendor dyno of its own part) + Forum
log_channel: Turbo Pressure vs Target (spool), EWG Position
notes: The owner's '~20 whp' has no dyno and likely includes a tune. Our cards keep +7 to +12 untuned (vendor) and catless +0-6.

finding: 'A downpipe changes the AFR and runs lean without a tune.'
basis: Forum vs Primary (KTuner staff: 'nothing in the tune you need to change to take advantage of exhaust modifications'; 'the tune covers exhaust mods') + Physics (air is metered at the MAF; the front A/F sensor is upstream of the downpipe)
log_channel: O2 vs target, STFT B1/LTFT B1
notes: What's true: a 200-cell or catless pipe sets a CEL, and a custom tune can use the pipe for more power. KTuner did ship a separate downpipe tune with changed cam commands, but for the FK8 Type R (civicxi-108, T3, not ours). Phearable 'accounting for the DP' is vendor practice, not a fuel need.

finding: KTuner staff don't recommend a vent-to-atmosphere blow-off valve. The MAF is upstream of the turbo, so venting metered air to atmosphere upsets fueling.
notes: Same physics as a boost leak (g3-13): metered air that never reaches the cylinders makes it rich.

finding: Which parts need a retune: intake housing changes, 4-bar MAP sensors and bigger turbos do. Intercooler, charge pipes and turbo inlet pipe can go on before a retune. The 27WON inlet pipe throws no CEL and needs no tune, with any gain coming from a tune. KTuner added 4-bar MAP support for the 11th-gen 1.5T in 1.0.11.7.
basis: Pro tuner + Primary (KTuner version history) + vendor claim via owner
ktuner_setting: MAF Scaling preset; 4 Bar Map Sensor option
notes: Gives the Install step a rule: only a housing change (or MAP sensor or turbo) needs a map change; the rest is a log-and-compare.

finding: Bigger turbos without a matching tune: expected lean in mid and upper boost, and aggressive boost from about 4,000 rpm (27WON on Si; advice to stay under 3,500 rpm until tuned). An untuned bigger turbo lost 12 wtq and spooled slower. Removing the electronic wastegate for a manual controller limits boost to wastegate spring pressure (~14 psi). 27WON's Gin turbo wants a 4-bar MAP sensor and a clutch.
notes: Stock turbo here.

finding: Clutch limits on manual cars: the stock clutch takes stock-ish tunes only; 13 % of tuned 11th gens have an upgraded clutch; a 10th gen on Hondata Stage 1+3 slipped its clutch.
notes: CVT car.

finding: What tuned owners fit (surveys): 11th gen: downpipe 46 %, intercooler 42 %, cold air intake 39 %, front pipe 23 %. 10th gen: downpipe 39 %, intake 53 %, intercooler 43 %, a race MAF on 27 % of aftermarket intakes. One owner ranks KTuner first, then intercooler and downpipe.
notes: Context for expectations: this owner's intake + DP + FP is the common setup.

finding: Vendor stage requirements: TSP Stage 2 needs a flex kit, a clutch and an intercooler. Phearable non-Si Stage 1.5 is factory-turbo only and not flex-compatible. Phearable 2.5 needs a clutch and a 0.5-4.5 V flex kit. Phearable's guide starts at KTuner + 1.5R (+64 hp / +99 tq), then a PRL intercooler for hot-weather consistency.
notes: Only the intercooler-for-heat order is relevant, and kc-heat-soak covers heat.

finding: PRL: the 11th-gen L15 head has dual exhaust ports (divided turbine inlet), while the 10th gen has a single port. 10th-gen exhaust and spool numbers don't carry over directly.
notes: kc-downpipe's '200-400 rpm earlier' is from Civic X dynos: add 'on the 10th gen, whose head differs'.

finding: A non-Integra 11th-gen hatch flowed less air than an Integra with similar mods, and the tuner couldn't explain why.
The 2025-26 Civic Si ECU (64B-AF1..AF4) can't be flashed over OBD from factory and needs the KTuner Connectivity Kit 1 at the ECU connectors.
notes: Si only. Check before applying to any 2025+ non-Si.

finding: Vendors hold base tunes back on purpose to protect the engine and CVT. TSP Stage 1 is 'slightly limited' and adds low-speed boost limiting for traction. TSP later cut Stage 2's low-end torque further. Hondata says damage comes from torque, not power.
kb_relation: confirms kc-table-boost (low-rpm torque hurts the CVT); confirms thresholds boost_raise_min_rpm

finding: Before the first full-throttle pull, wait until coolant is about 180 °F (82 °C) when there's no oil-temperature gauge. Run 91-93 octane on a 23 psi base map (87 won't do). Pre-flash advice: never run under the tune's minimum octane, never brake-launch a CVT, warm the engine fully.
basis: Primary (TSP about its own maps) + Forum
notes: Matches the brief's 80 °C checkpoint from an independent vendor source.

finding: Self-tuning risk: at least one engine failure in the reliability thread came from self-tuning, and 'one bad adjustment' can do serious damage. KTuner staff decline to teach VTEC, boost or cam tuning and refer owners to a professional.
notes: Supports the app's bounded families and forbidden_tables.

finding: Order with bolt-ons: custom tuning is best done after all parts are in. With a KTuner basemap, run it until the downpipe is fitted, then flash the vendor tune.
kb_relation: confirms knowledge/playbook.md 'intake' stage (parts written down first)

finding: Vendor tunes load into KTuner partly locked: many maps aren't visible or editable.
notes: Capabilities line: if the owner moves to a vendor file, the app can't read hidden tables, so Map tour and Flash plan go read-only for those families. Today's map (KTuner Starter) is open.

finding: Matched-pull test design: compare settings with everything else fixed (Throttle Responsiveness 3 with reduced rev hang, Advanced VSA factory, Turbo Responsiveness 3, Normal 18 / Sport 21 psi, all runs at 21 psi in 2nd gear).
notes: Manual gearbox.

finding: Rev limits and 2-step cut fuel. The closer the limit and restart rpm, the faster the cut; Honda's default spread is 200 rpm, and the low limit doubles as a basic 2-step. Anti-lag is launch-control ignition retard (start at -5°), race use only, and none is planned for the FK8.
The Type-R's Bosch ECU targets torque and is mapped beyond stock. Supporting a new boosted platform needs custom coding and the ECU part number.

VTEC: KTuner's Low/High Cam switch means low cam = VTEC off and high cam = VTEC on. The VTEC engagement window's crossover (mBar) has to be found by datalogging, and engaging VTEC changes manifold pressure.
kb_relation: extends kc-table-wot (Low and High cam tables)
log_channel: none (no cam-state channel on the owner's logger)

finding: On one platform an aftermarket wideband can only go into the PTANK or ELD input, which can't be graphed yet.
